Maintainable software architecture is characterized by several key principles:

## Clear Separation of Concerns
- Each component has a single, well-defined responsibility
- Business logic is separated from infrastructure concerns
- UI, data access, and business rules are kept in distinct layers

## Loose Coupling & High Cohesion
- Components depend on abstractions, not concrete implementations
- Related functionality is grouped together
- Changes in one area don't cascade throughout the system

## Consistent Patterns & Standards
- Uniform coding conventions and naming schemes
- Consistent error handling and logging approaches
- Standardized ways of solving similar problems

## Clear Dependencies
- Explicit dependency management (avoid hidden dependencies)
- Use of dependency injection where appropriate
- Well-defined interfaces between components

## Comprehensive Documentation
- Architecture decision records (ADRs) explaining key choices
- Clear API documentation
- Up-to-date diagrams showing system structure

## Testability
- Components can be tested in isolation
- Clear boundaries that enable unit and integration testing
- Testable interfaces and minimal external dependencies

## Modularity
- System is broken into logical, replaceable modules
- Clear module boundaries with well-defined APIs
- Ability to modify or replace modules without affecting others

## Evolutionary Design
- Architecture can adapt to changing requirements
- Refactoring-friendly structure
- Gradual improvement rather than big rewrites

The goal is code that developers can understand, modify, and extend without fear of breaking existing functionality.
